summary: Paolo Visigalli is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Padua, Sapienza University of Rome, and the University of Cambridge. He held a post at NYU Shanghai (~2020–2024) and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University (~2024).

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya (1891–1978) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He directed the Mithila Institute (~1954–1958) and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, and served as General Editor of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1961–1972).

Paride Stortini works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. A doctoral student at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), he has also served as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Parimal G. Patil is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard University (~1991–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–2002). He became a professor at Harvard University around 2001.

Parul Dave-Mukherji is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pascale Haag (b. 1965) works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (~1997–2002) and at Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay (~2013–2018), later holding a post at the EHESS (~2007).

Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania and served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).
Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Bristol and at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, where she became Professor Emerita in 1996, and has served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey (b. 1947) is a Sinology and history scholar. Educated at the University of Chicago and Columbia University, she taught at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1982, 1985) and served as Professor of History at the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister (b. 1953) is a Japanology and art history scholar. After earning her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas (~1976–1983), she held various curatorial and academic posts, including professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2007–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a Sinology and Tibetology scholar. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania supervised by Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister (b. 1979) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) under Helmut Krasser, and joined the Austrian Academy of Sciences and its IKGA around 2012.

Patrick Olivelle (b. 1942) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oxford (~1968–1972) and Penn (~1972–1974) under Ludo Rocher, later serving at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 1991).

Patrick Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman (attested 2004).
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2012).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a master and scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1830–1842) and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught many prominent disciples.

Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and at Emory University, where he is attested from 1998 and as Professor Emeritus by 2026.

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa (attested 1997) and other traditional teachers, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.
